diagnostic_scope.reason: large replay reports store aggregate summaries with rows=[], so pressure-segment rates require recomputing aggregate segment counters from public data mappings

interpretation.adapter_or_model_concern: No immediate production-model concern is proven. The main adapter concern is semantic: public proxy features are not calibrated decision-time simulator observations. Company replay is needed before treating low dispatch/action24/action32 as a model behavior issue.
interpretation.dispatch_opportunity_effect: The adapter often maps waits/service/order-pressure proxies into conservative feasible-dispatch and route context; the policy therefore prefers hold-style actions on public rows. This is descriptive, not a rollout failure.

distinctions.actual_env_rollout_performance: measured only by internal simulator scenario/gate/equal-budget evals, not by this replay
distinctions.company_historical_replay_needed: required for stronger claims about real dispatch/fleet/reorder decisions and OPE
distinctions.public_replay_descriptive_action_tendenc: what the production policy chooses on proxy states built from public rows

interpretation.missingness_effect: Olist has medium confidence and high missingness because route/fleet fields are absent; LaDe and NYC have high confidence by adapter rules but still proxy-only state reconstruction.
interpretation.primary_explanation: Low dispatch/action24/action32 is mostly expected because public rows are one-row proxy observations rather than full simulator decision-time states with current unassigned orders, feasible dispatch alternatives, secondary fleet availability, inventory state, route alternatives, and reward context.
